limits.counts: 'Main body of text (excluding abstract, tables/figures, and references) not to exceed 7,000 words.' (HTML guide, read 2026-11-16)
limits.notes: Heredity's Guide for Authors PDF, 'Revised 21/02/2023'. (Read 2026-11-14; the HTML guide below supersedes it.) Abstract: 'This should not exceed 250 words', on a separate page and also in the submission form. It should state the conceptual issue(s), the approach and the main findings. Display items: 'max. 8 figures or tables'. 'Composite figures containing more than three individual figures will count as two figures.' References: 'There should normally be no more than 100 references' (author-year style). Title page: 'A succinct title', and 'A running title of no more than 150 characters' with no abbreviations (the December 2021 guide said 50 characters). Original Articles contain, in order: cover letter (with a Conflict of Interest statement), title page, abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion, acknowledgements, author contribution statement, conflict of interest, data archiving (a section titled 'Data Archiving' is mandatory), references, figure legends, tables, and figures (uploaded separately). A graphical abstract is optional (9 cm wide x 5 cm high). Each supplementary file needs a text summary of no more than 50 words. Initial submissions may be 'in any recognised double-spaced format that includes line numbers'. No keywords are requested. 2026-11-16: the current HTML guide (https://www.nature.com/hdy/authors-and-referees/gta) was read and wins over the 2023 PDF: 'Title of the paper - succinct, informative, of 150 characters or less' (no running title on its title page); an unstructured abstract of at most 250 words, a main text of at most 7,000 words (not counting the abstract, tables, figures and references), at most 8 tables or figures, and at most 100 references; its component list adds a Research Ethics Statement after Data archiving.

sources.what: Heredity Guide for Authors PDF ('Revised 21/02/2023'). Read in full (text extracted locally).

Current HTML guide. Read 2026-11-16 (it answered with a cookies notice the first time on 2026-11-14). It is newer than the PDF and wins where they differ. Its component list: Cover letter, Title page, Abstract, Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Acknowledgements, Author contribution statement, Conflict of Interest, Data archiving, Research Ethics Statement, References, Figure legends.

evidence.status: read (the current HTML guide, read 2026-11-16; the 2023 PDF read 2026-11-14)

abstract.note: PDF: 'This should not exceed 250 words and should be provided on a separate page in the file, as well as on the online submission form.' No headings are prescribed. Abbreviations 'should be defined in full at their first usage in the Abstract'. Nothing on references.

front.name: Graphical abstract
front.note: 'Graphical Abstracts (optional)'; uploaded as a 'Figure' labelled 'Graphical abstract'; 9 cm wide x 5 cm high, minimum 300 dpi, white background.
The PDF asks for no keywords.

The current HTML guide's title page has no running title, only 'Title of the paper - succinct, informative, of 150 characters or less'. The 2023 PDF's 'running title of no more than 150 characters' is superseded.

author_contributions.heading: Author Contributions
author_contributions.where: after Acknowledgements, before Conflict of Interest (the component list calls it 'Author contribution statement')
author_contributions.quote: The statement can be up to several sentences long, describing the tasks of individual authors referred to by their initials.

funding.where: in Acknowledgements ('should include sources of support including sponsorship (e.g. grants, university, charity, commercial organisation)')

competing_interests.heading: Conflict of Interest
competing_interests.where: in the manuscript before the References, and also in the cover letter, on the title page and in the submission form
competing_interests.quote: These statements acknowledging or denying conflicts of interest must be included in the manuscript under the heading Conflict of Interest.
competing_interests.note: If none: 'the statement will simply read that the authors have nothing to disclose' (PDF). The HTML guide's component list says 'Conflict of Interest'; its paragraph on it is headed 'Competing Interests'.

data_availability.heading: Data Archiving
data_availability.where: own section after Conflict of Interest, before References
data_availability.quote: Original Articles must contain a section entitled 'Data Archiving' which specifies where the data used in the paper can be accessed.
data_availability.note: The component list writes 'Data archiving'; the paragraph and 'Articles must contain a section entitled ‘Data Archiving’' write it with a capital A.

code_availability.note: No heading. A paper describing new simulations or analytical methods must make the relevant software public, 'wherever possible'.

ethics.heading: Research Ethics Statement
ethics.where: own section after Data Archiving, before References (the HTML guide's component list)
ethics.note: HTML guide, read 2026-11-16. Under its 'Research Ethics Statement' heading it covers human and animal research (committee and reference number). The 2023 PDF had no such section.
ethics.quote: Ethics, author contributions and data availability statements are mandatory in all papers and must be included in the article files on submission.

acknowledgements.heading: Acknowledgements
acknowledgements.where: after Discussion; listed among the components original articles 'must contain'. The title page is submitted 'excluding acknowledgements'.

ai_use.where: Methods (or a suitable alternative part if there is no Methods)
ai_use.quote: Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (and if a Methods section is not available, in a suitable alternative part) of the manuscript.
ai_use.note: HTML guide, read 2026-11-16 (not in the 2023 PDF).
